newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-AUXERRE VICTORY VIRTUALLY BURIES RANGERS CUP HOPES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AUXERRE VICTORY VIRTUALLY BURIES RANGERS CUP HOPES.

text.p: Stand-in striker Thomas Deniaud scored twice as French champions Auxerre beat Rangers 2-1 and dealt the Scottish champions a potentially fatal Champions' League blow.
Deniaud, only playing because of injury to Lilian Laslandes, scored two second-half headers to give Guy Roux's French champions three points in Glasgow.
Rangers by contrast are pointless after two games and with back-to-back matches against Ajax to come, Walter Smith's side already look out of the running for the quarter-final places.
Paul Gascoigne marked his 50th appearance for Rangers with his 25th goal, and a yellow card, but he couldn't add to his 71st minute header.
More than 37,000 fans turned out in the hope of witnessing a first Champions' League victory for three-and-a-half years but now the Rangers run stands at ten matches without a win.
Czech referee Vaclav Krondl booked six players.
Incredibly, Deniaud's goals were his first for Auxerre, having twice been loaned to lower division clubs and having spent last year in the second division at Angers.
"I thought he might score a goal because he is good in the air," said Auxerre trainer Guy Roux, who used the 25-year-old Deniaud in place of the injured Lilian Laslandes.
Rangers manager Walter Smith said: "I thought we controlled most of the match.
"Auxerre defended well but we did not break them down. If you lose the type of goals we did it costs you dearly.
"We put in a lot of effort in the last 20 minutes but didn't really threaten apart from Gascoigne's goal. We are bottom and we are not particularly happy about it."

Rangers: 1-Andy Goram; 2-Alex Cleland, 3-Joerg Albertz, 4-Richard Gough, 6-Joachim Bjorklund, 8-Paul Gascoigne, 10-Gordon Durie (24-Ian Ferguson 85th), 11-Brian Laudrup, 17-Peter Van Vossen, 20-Derek McInnes, 23-Craig Moore (18-Erik Bo Andersen 78th).

Auxerre: 1-Lionel Charbonnier; 2-Alain Goma, 3-Franck Rabarivony, 6-Philippe Violeau, 7-Sabri Lamouchi, 8-Moussa Saib, 11-Bernard Diomede, 12-Taribo West, 13-Frederic Danjou, 14-Christian Henna, 18-Thomas Deniaud (10-Antoine Sibierski 86th).
